$comment: GET /users/me/token?type=onbehalf -- verified 2026-09-15 against Zoom's own Meeting SDK auth doc, its transition blog post, and independent third-party write-ups (Recall.ai, MeetStream), all agreeing on the shape. This CORRECTS the assumption this issue was filed under: the query value is `onbehalf`, never `obf` -- `type=obf` is not a value Zoom's docs use anywhere. Required since Zoom's own enforcement date (23 Feb 2026, not 2 Mar as one third-party source states -- Zoom's own blog is the one trusted here) for a Meeting SDK bot joining a meeting it did not create. The token is scoped to ONE meeting and cannot be reused across meetings, so `meetingId` is required on every mint rather than cached from a previous call.
title: Mint on-behalf-of token
description: Mint a short-lived token so a bot can join a Zoom meeting on the authorising user's behalf.
$idempotencyComment: Zoom's own description calls this a short-lived, SINGLE-USE token. A retry mints a second one rather than returning the first -- harmless to mint twice, but never a call worth reusing a stored idempotency key for, which is why this is unsafe-to-replay rather than idempotent.

request.$pathComment: `me` refers to the user whose OAuth access token is on the request -- the same account that authorised the app with user:read:token. Zoom's docs also show a userId path form; `me` is the one every reviewed source actually used and removes a way to ask for the wrong account's token by typing an id.

config.label: Meeting ID
config.description: The meeting the bot is about to join. The minted token works for this meeting only.

outputShape.description: The OBF token. Present it the way the Meeting SDK's join call expects; it is not a Bearer header value on Zoom's REST API.
